articles.title: Elders drive recycling change in Dominican Republic Rivera
articles.subtitle: Older residents in Santo Domingo's Rivera community turn recycling into cleaner streets, food aid, and renewed purpose

images.description: Recipients listen to sharing from volunteers before entering the church one by one to receive food packages. | Photo: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic
images.note: Main featured image - shows food distribution event

images.description: LEFT: Twice a week, Adelina opens her yard so neighbors can store collected bottles there until there are enough for the truck to pick up. CENTER: Residents first keep collected bottles at home, then bring them to a fixed point every Thursday for the recycling truck. RIGHT: At Escuela República de Costa Rica students bring plastic and PET bottles to school for recycling. | Photos: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic
images.note: Three-panel comparison showing recycling collection methods

images.description: LEFT: Twice a week, Adelina opens her yard so neighbors can store collected bottles until the truck arrives. RIGHT: Dental outreach provides oral care to the recycling volunteers. | Photo: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic
images.note: Two-panel image showing community storage and health care services

images.description: LEFT: For Mother's Day in May, a mental wellness session and small raffle were held for the recycling volunteers. RIGHT: Before school started, backpacks and stationery were given to the children and grandchildren of recycling volunteers. | Photos: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic
images.note: Two-panel image showing wellness activities and school supply distribution

images.description: LEFT: The food distribution site was chosen at a church near Rivera, making it easy for residents to attend. RIGHT: Tents were set up in the open space outside the church so recycling volunteers could hear a summary of the year's recycling results and learn more about Tzu Chi. | Photos: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic
images.note: Two-panel image showing distribution venue setup

images.description: Every Thursday is now also vegetarian day, encouraging recycling volunteers to protect the Earth through their food choices as well. | Photo: Tzu Chi Dominican Republic

articles.title: Bringing Relief to the Highlands in Manabao, Dominican Republic
articles.subtitle: Medical outreach and food aid bring relief and hope to remote mountain communities in Manabao, Dominican Republic

images.description: Volunteers distributing food supplies to remote mountain communities of Manabao in the Dominican Republic. | Photo: Tzu Chi Dominicana
images.note: Main featured image - shows food aid distribution in mountains

images.description: Volunteers cross a suspension bridge to reach remote families in Manabao, La Vega, ensuring that even the most isolated residents are not forgotten. | Photo: Aliocy
images.note: Shows volunteers crossing suspension bridge - illustrates remote access challenge

images.description: Two hundred and fifty food packages were prepared for distribution to recipients who are mostly elderly or families with health challenges. | Photo: Mariana Ju
images.note: Shows preparation of food packages for distribution

images.description: Lisa, age 15, received her first dental checkup thanks to the outreach, addressing a painful cavity and learning about oral health. | Photo: Carlos Yang (楊卡羅斯)
images.note: Shows first-time dental care for young patient - illustrates medical services

images.description: Mariana Ju (front, holding microphone) introduces the Bamboo Bank tradition to local residents, encouraging a culture of giving and mutual support. | Photo: Raymond
images.note: Shows community education about giving and support programs
